articles.title: Nafisa Ali Shares Health Update as She Begins Targeted Therapy
articles.excerpt: The veteran actress told followers on Instagram that a PET/CT scan showed new deposits on her liver, and that her medical team has moved her onto targeted therapy.
articles.image_caption: Nafisa Ali smiles at an event, wearing a red saree with a decorative blue border and gold jewelry. The veteran Bollywood actress has shared that her Stage 4 cancer has progressed and she is beginning targeted therapy.
articles.nri_angle: For many in the Indian diaspora facing cancer in their own families, Ali's plain-spoken public updates have become a touchstone — a well-known face describing scans, protocols and setbacks in language other patients recognize.

articles.title: Bollywood's Biggest Stars Turn Out for Ambani Family Ganpati Celebrations
articles.excerpt: The Ambani family's Ganesh Chaturthi celebration at Antilia on September 14 drew a who's-who of Bollywood and cricket, with stars from Salman Khan to Alia Bhatt arriving for the evening's aarti.

articles.title: Amitabh Bachchan Dismisses Retirement Talk After Late-Night Blog Sparks Frenzy
articles.excerpt: The 83-year-old described hosting KBC 18 as a 'heart-breaking experience' before signing off with 'I wish to retire now' — a line that set off a frenzy he later brushed aside.
articles.image_caption: Amitabh Bachchan. The actor dismissed talk of retirement following his latest public appearance.

articles.title: Mirzapur The Movie a Clean Hit on Day 10, Enters 2026's Top 5 Grossers
articles.excerpt: Ten days in, the Prime Video spin-off has collected ₹189.67 crore net in India on a ₹90 crore budget — a 110.74% return on investment that trade trackers call a clean hit, making it Bollywood's fourth such verdict of 2026.
articles.image_caption: The theatrical poster for Mirzapur The Movie, the film offshoot of the Prime Video series. The film secured a clean hit verdict on day 10 of its theatrical run with a 110.74% return on investment.
articles.nri_angle: The film's overseas markets, led by North America and the Middle East, have contributed about ₹46 crore by day 10 — roughly a fifth of its worldwide gross — as diaspora audiences turned a streaming-known property into a theatrical draw.

articles.title: How to Watch the Emmys in India: Time, Channels and Top Nominees
articles.excerpt: The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards air on September 14 in the US — and stream live in India in the early hours of September 15 on JioHotstar. Here's the full timing, the nominees to watch, and the Indian names in the mix.
articles.image_caption: The Emmy statuette in artwork for the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards. The ceremony airs in India on September 15, with the red carpet at 4:30 AM IST and the main show at 5:30 AM IST, streaming live on JioHotstar.

articles.title: Ramayana's First Song 'Jai Jai Ram' Wins Fans, Praised For Visual Upgrades

articles.image_caption: Stills from Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana show Ranbir Kapoor as Ram and Sai Pallavi as Sita. The film's first song 'Jai Jai Ram' drew praise online for its upgraded visuals.

articles.title: 'Main Na Raha Mera' First Look: Adhyayan Suman's Musical Romance Sets Teaser for September 16

articles.title: Bollywood Takes Over BRICS: Anwar Ibrahim and an Indonesian Journalist Sing Hindi Classics in Delhi
articles.excerpt: The Malaysian prime minister sang a Kishore Kumar classic at a BRICS gala dinner while an Indonesian journalist performed a 1990s hit — as serious diplomacy, including an upgraded India-Malaysia partnership, moved forward offstage.
articles.image_caption: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim sings at a piano during a BRICS gala dinner in New Delhi. He performed Kishore Kumar's 1965 classic "Khwab Ho Tum Ya Koi Haqeeqat" from the film Teen Devian.

articles.title: Ralph Lauren Faces Backlash for Uncredited Zardozi Gown at Fashion Week
articles.excerpt: A Spring 2027 gown shown in New York was described by the brand as having "hand-applied embellishments" — with no mention of India or zardozi. Critics say this is how global fashion erases the artisans behind the work.
articles.image_caption: A close-up shows bead-and-thread embroidery on a pink Ralph Lauren gown, shown beside the gown worn on the runway. Critics identified the work as zardozi after the brand described it only as 'hand-applied embellishments.'
articles.nri_angle: The diaspora sits at the center of this debate — Indian-American designers and consumers have been among the loudest voices demanding global brands name the crafts they borrow.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Diljit Dosanjh Makes History as First Punjabi Singer to Headline Wembley
articles.excerpt: The Aura World Tour stop drew some 90,000 fans, free turban-tying on site, and a surprise Ahmedabad stadium announcement — with ZEE5 branding the road to the arch.
articles.image_caption: Diljit Dosanjh performs on stage in a white kurta and black vest during his Aura World Tour concert. He headlined London's Wembley Stadium on September 12, 2026, becoming the first Punjabi singer to top the bill at the venue.
articles.nri_angle: For the British Punjabi diaspora, the Wembley headline was a hometown milestone — a Punjabi-language artist filling the venue of Michael Jackson and Queen, with British fans telling the BBC he is "that level" for them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Hindi Films and Series Arriving This Week: Daayra to Lust Stories 3
articles.excerpt: September 14–20 brings a crowded Friday, September 18, with three theatrical releases including Meghna Gulzar's Daayra, plus Netflix's Lust Stories 3 and Rohit Sharma's TV hosting debut.
articles.image_caption: The auditorium of the Star Theatre in Kolkata. Five Hindi films and series arrive between September 14 and 20, led by Meghna Gulzar's crime thriller Daayra.

articles.title: Keerthy Suresh Brings Contemporary Kanjivaram to TIFF 2026 Dorothy Premiere
articles.excerpt: The actor walked the Toronto red carpet in a burgundy-and-gold Kanjivaram-inspired ensemble for the world premiere of her Tamil drama Dorothy, which earned a standing ovation in the festival's Centrepiece section.
articles.image_caption: Keerthy Suresh poses on the red carpet at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival in a burgundy and antique-gold contemporary Kanjivaram-inspired ensemble. She attended the world premiere of her Tamil film Dorothy, directed by Karthik Subbaraj, which earned a standing ovation at the festival.
articles.nri_angle: Toronto is home to one of North America's largest South Asian communities, and the Dorothy premiere gives diaspora audiences an early festival encounter with a Tamil film before its September 25 theatrical release.

articles.title: AR Rahman Pitches Kashmir as Global Cinema Hub, Urges Bollywood to Film There
articles.excerpt: The Oscar-winning composer told ANI in Srinagar that Bollywood should project Kashmir's beauty and peace rather than its troubled past, praising the International Film Festival of Jammu and Kashmir as a launchpad for global recognition.
articles.image_caption: AR Rahman speaks to media personnel holding microphones in Srinagar. The Oscar-winning composer urged Bollywood to film more in Kashmir and praised the International Film Festival of Jammu and Kashmir as a commendable initiative.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora, Kashmir is one of the most emotionally resonant destinations in the subcontinent, and a Bollywood revival in the Valley championed by Rahman gives that longing a contemporary soundtrack.

articles.title: Dorothy and Termite: Oscar Breakouts Chart New Course for Indian Cinema at TIFF
articles.excerpt: Oscar-winner Guneet Monga Kapoor premiered the Tamil gangster western “Dorothy” to a standing ovation at TIFF 2026 — her first project under Jio Studios' majority stake — while documentarian Shaunak Sen unveiled his fiction debut “Termite.”
articles.image_caption: Two men walk through a narrow rural street lined with old stone houses in a still from the Tamil-language film Dorothy. The Karthik Subbaraj-directed film premiered to a standing ovation at the Toronto International Film Festival this week.
articles.nri_angle: TIFF sits in a city with one of the world's largest South Asian diasporas, and a Tamil-language premiere backed by studio money tests whether festival prestige for Indian independent cinema can convert into diaspora box office worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mirzapur The Movie Crosses $2 Million In North America, Climbing Indian Box Office Charts
articles.excerpt: The crime thriller took ₹9.5 crore on its second Friday to reach ₹163.27 crore net in India, overtaking Awarapan 2 for the year's No. 6 spot, while its $2.05 million North American haul made it the fourth Bollywood film of 2026 to cross $2 million in the territory.
articles.nri_angle: Mirzapur The Movie's $2.05 million North American first week — Bollywood's fourth $2M grosser of 2026 — shows how diaspora demand for established Indian series IPs converts directly into overseas box office.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sardar 2 opens at Rs 5.30 crore, loses domestic battle to Soori's Mandaadi
articles.excerpt: Karthi's Sardar 2 grossed Rs 5.30 crore in India on opening day but was out-earned at home by the much smaller Soori-starrer Mandaadi, which managed Rs 5.55 crore on nearly 1,000 fewer shows. Overseas business gave the sequel a narrow worldwide lead.
articles.image_caption: Karthi, who stars in Sardar 2. The film opened at Rs 5.30 crore domestically, trailing Soori's Mandaadi in its first week.
articles.nri_angle: Overseas business was the one front where Sardar 2 led on day one, with Tamil diaspora audiences in the Gulf, Malaysia and Singapore turning out for Karthi's sequel.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Toxic week 2: Yash's film crawls to Rs 263 crore as 300-crore flop looms
articles.excerpt: Yash's Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups added just Rs 6.75 crore in its second weekend, taking its 12-day India gross to Rs 263 crore. Trade trackers say the costly film is headed for one of the biggest losses in Indian cinema.
articles.image_caption: A still from Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups, showing Yash and Kiara Advani. The Geethu Mohandas-directed film reached Rs 263 crore gross in India after 12 days and is expected to finish its run under Rs 270 crore.
articles.nri_angle: The film's English version, aimed partly at overseas multiplex audiences, was pulled after a week, and the theatrical collapse leaves the digital premiere as diaspora viewers' main route to the film.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Don't Be Shy trailer drops: Alia Bhatt's coming-of-age rom-com bets on fresh faces
articles.excerpt: The first trailer for Prime Video's Don't Be Shy introduces four debutant leads headed by Aarushi Bajaj, as producers Alia Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt back a young-adult story of first love, friendship and messy choices ahead of its September 25 premiere.
articles.image_caption: A collage of the four young leads of Don't Be Shy alongside producers Alia Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt. The coming-of-age romantic comedy premieres on Prime Video on September 25, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: The September 25 day-and-date Prime Video release across 240+ countries brings the film to diaspora living rooms worldwide at the same time as India.

articles.title: From Mardaani to Delhi Crime: Hindi Cinema's Women Cops Take Charge
articles.excerpt: Rani Mukerji's franchise completed an unprecedented hattrick of hits, while streaming turned Shefali Shah, Sonakshi Sinha and Raveena Tandon into television's most compelling investigators.
articles.image_caption: Actor Rani Mukerji, whose Shivani Shivaji Roy in the Mardaani franchise is Hindi cinema's defining woman cop. Mardaani 3 closed its 2026 theatrical run at about Rs 77 crore, the series' best.
articles.nri_angle: Streaming made these performances global by default — Delhi Crime topped charts in 10 countries, giving NRI audiences a second front of Indian storytelling beyond Bollywood tentpoles.

articles.title: Swara Bhasker on Bollywood's Evolution: The Khans, OTT and the Industry's Reckoning
articles.excerpt: In a series of candid interviews, the actor weighs in on Salman Khan's mentorship, streaming's levelling of stardom, the boycott-era slump and the industry's storytelling habits.
articles.image_caption: Actor Swara Bhasker. In a new interview she reflects on Bollywood's evolution, the Khans' three-decade dominance and the streaming era's reshaping of stardom.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora audiences now watch Hindi cinema primarily on streaming, making Bhasker's argument that OTT has 'democratised stardom' a direct description of how NRIs experience Bollywood.

articles.title: Hollywood and Regional Hits Squeeze Bollywood's Share Below 40 Percent in 2026
articles.excerpt: India's box office is headed for a record year, but Ormax data shows Hindi cinema ceding ground to a ₹500-crore Spider-Man and surging Telugu and Tamil releases.
articles.image_caption: Shenoy's Theatre in Kochi, Kerala. India's domestic box office grew 13 percent through July 2026, but Hindi cinema's share has slipped below 40 percent for the first time.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora moviegoers mirror the shift, filling overseas multiplexes for Spider-Man and Telugu/Tamil blockbusters that now share screens once dominated by Hindi tentpoles.

articles.image_caption: Sharat Saxena at a film event. Saxena has shared photos of his standing MRI scan ahead of lumbar spine surgery.

articles.title: AR Rahman Was Told Not to Work With Danny Boyle — He Won Two Oscars Instead
articles.excerpt: Warned that Danny Boyle might throw out his score, Rahman composed the Slumdog Millionaire music in secret over three weeks — and collected two Oscars, two Grammys, a Golden Globe and a BAFTA.
articles.image_caption: AR Rahman holds a vintage microphone against a blue backdrop. Rahman has recalled that his agent warned him against scoring Slumdog Millionaire — he composed it in secret in three weeks and won two Oscars.
articles.nri_angle: An iconic Indian-artist-on-world-stage story — the diaspora takes pride in Rahman's Oscars and the 'Jai Ho' cultural moment, and the trust-your-instincts arc is strong human interest.

articles.title: Rani Mukerji Accepts Raj Kapoor Award in Marathi, Marks Three Decades in Cinema
articles.excerpt: The actor received the Raj Kapoor Special Contribution Award at the 62nd Maharashtra State Film Awards, where she spoke in Marathi about Mumbai and Maharashtra shaping her identity and career.

articles.title: 'Why Are Kashmiri Actors Always Terrorists?': Bollywood's Typecasting Debate
articles.excerpt: Filmmakers and critics say Hindi cinema keeps casting Kashmiri performers in one role — the militant — and rarely lets them play anything else.

articles.title: The 'Carbon Copy' Film That Pakistan Banned: The Story of Bedari and Jagriti
articles.excerpt: Pakistan's 1957 patriotic hit Bedari was a scene-for-scene copy of India's Jagriti — and once audiences realised, the ban triggered an uproar.
articles.image_caption: India's 1954 patriotic classic Jagriti, a beloved film about a young reformer's journey. Pakistan's 1957 Urdu film Bedari was later exposed as a scene-for-scene copy of it, and banned after audiences found out.
articles.nri_angle: The Bedari-Jagriti saga is a beloved anecdote of the subcontinent's shared film heritage, resonating with diaspora audiences nostalgic for the pre-Partition cultural world.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Karnataka High Court Grants Actor Duniya Vijay Divorce, Orders Rs 2 Crore Alimony
articles.excerpt: A division bench dissolved the actor's 27-year marriage on grounds of cruelty, overturning a Bengaluru family court ruling, and ordered a Rs 2 crore one-time settlement within two months.
articles.image_caption: Kannada actor Duniya Vijay. The Karnataka High Court has granted him divorce, ordering Rs 2 crore in alimony.
articles.nri_angle: Kannada and Indian diaspora audiences follow Sandalwood legal dramas closely, and the Rs 2 crore figure will be read as a benchmark in celebrity divorce settlements.
